mainTopic: When an אתרוג or סוכה used for the מצוה becomes permitted at the end of סוכות (including in חוץ לארץ), opened by an aggadah about Torah 'filling' a person
overview: The amud opens by finishing an aggadic lesson. A human vessel holds more only when it is empty, but with הקדוש ברוך הוא the full person holds more. This is learned from the doubled verb 'אם שמוע תשמע': listening leads to more listening, and reviewing the old leads to learning the new. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's line that children eat their אתרוגים right after the seventh-day מצוה. רבי יוחנן forbids the אתרוג all of the seventh day, and the סוכה even on the eighth. ריש לקיש permits the אתרוג once the מצוה is done. Their dispute is whether the אתרוג was set aside only for its מצוה or for the whole day. The same משנה is used in two versions of a challenge between them, and אביי explains why רבי יוחנן treats the סוכה, which is needed at בין השמשות, more strictly than the אתרוג. The גמרא then brings further views from לוי, אבוה דשמואל and רבי זירא, two teachings of רבי זירא about children, and a parallel dispute between רב and רב אסי. In חוץ לארץ the הלכה follows אביי: the אתרוג is forbidden on the eighth day and permitted on the ninth. Finally, רב and רבי יוחנן discuss how to treat the doubtful eighth day for the סוכה and for the ברכה; everyone agrees we sit in the סוכה, and the exact dispute continues on the next amud.

steps.title: God's measure: a full vessel holds more
steps.stepSummary: Finishing a teaching that contrasts human vessels with the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא: with God, the full one holds more and the empty one holds nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: [With human vessels, an empty one] holds things, and a full one does not hold. But the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is the opposite: a full one holds, and an empty one does not hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an aggadic lesson that started on the previous amud. It contrasts how normal containers work with how הקדוש ברוך הוא works with people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A physical cup can only take more if it is empty. With Torah and wisdom it is the reverse: a person already full of knowledge can absorb more, while an 'empty' person cannot hold on to what he is given.

keyTerms.meaning: the way (measure) of the Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words right before it say that with a human vessel, an empty vessel holds. So 'מחזיק' at the very start belongs to that human-vessel half of the contrast.

phrases.english: [an empty vessel] holds; a full one does not hold.
phrases.notes: This wraps up the comparison of people to vessels that began earlier.

phrases.english: But the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is:
a full one holds; an empty one does not hold,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the aggadic teaching from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spiritually, someone already filled with Torah can take in more; an empty person cannot retain it.

steps.title: Proof from the verse: if you listen, you will keep listening
steps.stepSummary: The doubled verb 'שמוע תשמע' teaches that one who listens now will continue to listen, and one who does not will not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And it will be, if you will surely listen (שמוע תשמע)...' If you listen, you will listen. And if not, you will not listen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to support the idea that a 'full' person keeps gaining more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah doubles the verb 'listen' (שמוע תשמע). The דרשה reads this as cause and effect: listening now leads to listening later. By the same reading, not listening leads to losing the ability to listen.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a verse)
'surely listen' – a doubled verb, read here as two stages

phrases.english: as it is said: 'And it will be, if you will surely listen, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים כח:א

phrases.english: 'If you listen' – 'you will listen' [further].
phrases.notes: Listening now leads to listening in the future.

phrases.english: And if not – you will not listen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a 'full' person keeps receiving more
steps.raayaSupportSource: The doubled verb in 'אם שמוע תשמע' (דברים כח:א)

steps.title: Another reading: review the old to gain the new
steps.stepSummary: A second reading of the פסוק: reviewing old learning lets you acquire new learning, and a heart that turns away loses the ability to listen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'If you listen' – to the old; 'you will listen' – to the new. 'And if your heart turns away' – you will no longer listen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to read the same doubled verb. Here it is applied to reviewing what you already learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this דבר אחר, the first 'listen' means reviewing old material and the second means acquiring new material. A second פסוק, 'ואם יפנה לבבך', describes the opposite: someone who turns away loses even the ability to keep learning.
steps.whatToRemember: With Torah, review is the key to growth. Someone who keeps up with what he already learned will gain new learning. Someone who neglects it loses the capacity to learn.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
'If you listen' – to the old,
'you will listen' – to the new.
'And if your heart turns away' – you will no longer listen.
phrases.notes: דברים ל:יז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the same verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reviewing old learning enables new learning; turning away ends one's ability to learn.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about children eating their אתרוגים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's statement that right after the מצוה on the seventh day, children eat their אתרוגים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] 'Immediately, children, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the משנה to open a new discussion about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that on the seventh day of סוכות, right after the מצוה, children unbind their לולבים and eat their אתרוגים. The question this raises is whether adults may also eat theirs that same day.

phrases.english: 'Immediately, children, etc.'
phrases.notes: A heading quoting the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה says children eat their אתרוגים immediately after the seventh-day מצוה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the אתרוג is forbidden on the seventh day, the סוכה even on the eighth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that one may not benefit from the אתרוג on the seventh day, only on the eighth. The סוכה stays forbidden even on the eighth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: An אתרוג on the seventh day is forbidden; on the eighth it is permitted. A סוכה is forbidden even on the eighth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן states his rule about when one may use or eat the אתרוג and the wood of the סוכה at the end of the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the אתרוג is 'set aside' (מוקצה) for the entire seventh day, so it may be eaten only on the eighth. The סוכה is different because it was in use until nightfall, including בין השמשות, the twilight that begins the eighth day. Since it was set aside at that moment, the ban carries through the whole eighth day.

keyTerms.meaning: citron, one of the ארבעה מינים

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the סוכה and the אתרוג follow the same timing. The אתרוג's מצוה is done only by day, so its ban ends with the seventh day. The סוכה was still needed at twilight into the eighth, so its ban extends through the eighth day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
An etrog on the seventh day is forbidden,
on the eighth it is permitted.
A sukkah is forbidden even on the eighth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֶתְרוֹג בַּשְּׁבִיעִי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an אמורא's ruling relating to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אתרוג is forbidden all of the seventh day and permitted on the eighth; the סוכה is forbidden even on the eighth.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the אתרוג is permitted even on the seventh day
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש disagrees: once the מצוה is done, the אתרוג may be eaten even on the seventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: An אתרוג is permitted even on the seventh day as well.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the opposing view about the אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He argues only about the אתרוג. Once the person has used it for the מצוה, nothing stops him from eating it that same day.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, רבי יוחנן's study partner

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
An etrog is permitted even on the seventh as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי יוחנן's ruling on the אתרוג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אתרוג may be eaten on the seventh day once the מצוה is fulfilled.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying principle divides רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the dispute. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the אתרוג is restricted while it is needed for the מצוה. The question is what idea makes one of them extend that restriction past the moment the מצוה is done.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind steps 5 and 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the dispute over eating the אתרוג on the seventh day.

steps.title: Set aside for its מצוה, or for the whole day?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds the אתרוג was set aside only for its מצוה. רבי יוחנן holds it was set aside for the entire day.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: it was set aside [only] for its מצוה. And the other master holds: it was set aside for the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the dispute. The two sides disagree about how long the אתרוג counts as 'set aside' (מוקצה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the restriction exists only to protect the מצוה, so it ends once the מצוה is done. For רבי יוחנן, designating the אתרוג for the day's מצוה reserves it for the entire day, so it stays forbidden until the day ends.
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute comes down to one question. Is the אתרוג reserved only for the act of the מצוה (ריש לקיש) or for the whole day of the מצוה (רבי יוחנן)?

phrases.english: One master holds: it was set aside for its מצוה,
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש

phrases.english: and the other master holds: it was set aside for the whole day.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש: the אתרוג is set aside only for the מצוה. רבי יוחנן: it is set aside for the whole day.

steps.title: ריש לקיש challenges from the משנה: children eat their אתרוגים right away
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש cites the משנה, where children eat their אתרוגים immediately, and argues that adults may do the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש objected to רבי יוחנן: 'Immediately, children unbind their לולבים and eat their אתרוגים.' Isn't it the same for adults?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's view using the words of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows אתרוגים being eaten on the seventh day, right after the מצוה. ריש לקיש assumes children are mentioned only as an example and adults are the same. If so, the אתרוג is not forbidden for the whole day, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection to him (from a תנאי source)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish objected to Rabbi Yochanan:
'Immediately, children unbind their lulavim
and eat their etrogim.'
Is it not that the same applies to adults!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's position, now that the root of the dispute has been explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the אתרוג is forbidden all of the seventh day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows אתרוגים eaten right after the seventh-day מצוה. If adults are included, the אתרוג is set aside only for the מצוה, not the whole day.

steps.title: No, the משנה means children specifically
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה's permission applies only to children, not to adults.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, children specifically.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן deflects the challenge. The משנה's case is limited to children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children are not obligated in the מצוה מן התורה, so their אתרוגים were never fully set aside for the day. Adults' אתרוגים, however, are set aside for the entire day. So the משנה does not contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's view survives this challenge. The משנה's permission to eat the אתרוג right away is limited to children, while adults must wait until the eighth day.

phrases.english: No, children specifically.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers only to children.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Children were mentioned as an example, and adults are the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only children may eat right away. Adults' אתרוגים remain set aside all of the seventh day.

steps.title: Second version: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the children
steps.stepSummary: In an alternate version of the exchange, רבי יוחנן uses the משנה about children eating their אתרוגים to challenge ריש לקיש. He reads it as saying only children may eat, not adults.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it went like this: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש from the משנה: 'Right away, the children take apart their לולבים and eat their אתרוגים.' So children, yes, but adults, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the argument about the משנה. This time the roles are reversed, and רבי יוחנן is the one attacking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Steps 9-10), ריש לקיש used the משנה as a proof. Here רבי יוחנן uses the very same משנה against ריש לקיש. He points out that the משנה mentions only children, so it seems adults may not eat their אתרוג on the seventh day.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (introduces a second version of a discussion)
He challenged him from an authoritative source

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Steps 9-10. There, ריש לקיש attacked using the משנה. In this second version, רבי יוחנן attacks with the same משנה. It is the same text, used in opposite directions.

phrases.english: Some say:
phrases.notes: Here comes a different version of the conversation we just saw.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan challenged Reish Lakish:
Immediately the children pull apart their lulavim
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: and eat their etrogim.
Children, yes; adults, no!
phrases.notes: This is the point the question is built on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the exchange of Steps 9-10 in reverse, with רבי יוחנן as the challenger
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the אתרוג may be eaten right after the מצוה, even on the seventh day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה permits eating only for children. This implies that adults may not eat, which contradicts ריש לקיש.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the משנה just describes what usually happens
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that adults may also eat their אתרוג. The משנה mentions children only because they are the ones who typically do this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same law applies even to adults. The reason the משנה mentions children is that it describes the usual way things happen.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself. He says the word 'children' in the משנה is not meant to exclude adults.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש rejects the inference 'children yes, adults no.' He explains that the משנה describes the common situation: children are eager to eat their אתרוגים right away. The law itself is the same for everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'אורחא דמלתא קתני' is a common tool throughout ש"ס. It explains that a detail in a משנה describes the typical case and does not set a legal limit.

phrases.english: The same is true even for adults,
and the reason it teaches 'children'
is that it teaches the usual way of things.
phrases.notes: Children typically eat their אתרוגים right away

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a detail in the משנה as describing the typical case rather than setting a legal limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'children' excludes adults, so adults may not eat their אתרוג
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'children' only describes the common case. Adults may also eat after the מצוה.

steps.title: רב פפא asks why a סוכה and an אתרוג are treated differently
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: according to רבי יוחנן, why is the סוכה forbidden even into the eighth day, while the אתרוג is permitted on the eighth day?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: According to רבי יוחנן, what is different about a סוכה, and what is different about an אתרוג?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about רבי יוחנן's view. The question sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that both the סוכה and the אתרוג are set aside for מצוה use. However, the סוכה stays forbidden even on שמיני עצרת, while the אתרוג becomes permitted on the eighth day. רב פפא wants to know the reason for this difference.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
According to Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא סוּכָּה, מַאי שְׁנָא אֶתְרוֹג?
phrases.english: what is different about a sukkah, and what is different about an etrog?
phrases.notes: The סוכה is forbidden even on the eighth day, while the אתרוג is not

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא סוּכָּה, מַאי שְׁנָא אֶתְרוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the children's אתרוגים to comparing the סוכה with the אתרוג according to רבי יוחנן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן extends the סוכה's restriction into the eighth day but does not do the same for the אתרוג

steps.title: אביי: the סוכה is still usable at twilight, but the אתרוג is not
steps.stepSummary: The סוכה can still be needed at בין השמשות of the seventh day, so it is set aside then. Because of the מיגו, it stays set aside for the whole eighth day. The אתרוג has no use at twilight, so it is never set aside for the eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: A סוכה is usable at twilight. If a meal happens to come up then, a person must sit and eat inside it. So it is set aside for twilight, and since it is set aside for twilight, it is set aside for the whole eighth day. An אתרוג is not usable at twilight, so it is not set aside for twilight, and not for the whole eighth day.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the difference. Everything depends on whether the item still has a מצוה use during בין השמשות at the end of the seventh day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בין השמשות might still be the seventh day, so someone eating then must eat in the סוכה. This makes the סוכה set aside at that moment. Since that moment might already be the eighth day, the restriction carries over for the entire eighth day (מיגו). The מצוה of the אתרוג is done only by day, so at twilight it has no use, and the restriction never reaches the eighth day.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight; a period of doubt whether it is day or night
It became set aside (מוקצה) for the מצוה
Since (once a status applies at one point, it extends further)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the סוכה is forbidden on שמיני עצרת because it is still needed at בין השמשות of the seventh day. The אתרוג is not needed then, so it is permitted on the eighth day.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A sukkah, which is fit for use at twilight,
since if a meal happens to come up for him
phrases.notes: At twilight at the end of the seventh day

phrases.english: he must sit inside it and eat inside it,
it is set aside for twilight,
and since it is set aside for twilight,
it is set aside for the entire eighth day.
phrases.notes: Twilight may already be the eighth day

phrases.english: An etrog, which is not fit for use at twilight,
phrases.notes: Its מצוה is done only by day

phrases.english: is not set aside for twilight,
and is not set aside for the entire eighth day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question from Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The סוכה still has a מצוה use at בין השמשות, so it is set aside then and, through מיגו, for the whole eighth day. The אתרוג has no use at twilight, so its restriction ends with the seventh day.

steps.title: לוי and אבוה דשמואל disagree about the אתרוג on the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: לוי says the אתרוג is forbidden even on the eighth day. אבוה דשמואל says it is forbidden on the seventh day but permitted on the eighth.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said: An אתרוג is forbidden even on the eighth day. אבוה דשמואל said: An אתרוג is forbidden on the seventh day and permitted on the eighth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement between two אמוראים about how long the אתרוג stays forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי treats the אתרוג like the סוכה and extends the restriction into the eighth day. אבוה דשמואל holds like רבי יוחנן as אביי explained: forbidden through the seventh day, permitted on the eighth.

phrases.english: And Levi said:
An etrog is forbidden even on the eighth day,
and the father of Shmuel said:
An etrog is forbidden on the seventh day, permitted on the eighth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵוִי אָמַר: אֶתְרוֹג אֲפִילּוּ בַּשְּׁמִינִי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another disagreement about whether the אתרוג's restriction extends into the eighth day
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי: the אתרוג is forbidden even on the eighth day. אבוה דשמואל: forbidden on the seventh day, permitted on the eighth.

steps.title: Who later followed which view
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל later changed his mind and adopted לוי's view. רבי זירא adopted אבוה דשמואל's original view.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבוה דשמואל took up the position of לוי, and רבי זירא took up the position of אבוה דשמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that positions shifted: אבוה דשמואל switched to לוי's view, while רבי זירא adopted אבוה דשמואל's original view. The next step proves the claim about רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבוה דשמואל retracted and now forbids the אתרוג even on the eighth day. His earlier view, permitting it on the eighth day, did not disappear, because רבי זירא held it.

keyTerms.meaning: He took up the position of

phrases.english: The father of Shmuel took up the position of Levi,

phrases.aramaic: קָם רַבִּי זֵירָא בְּשִׁיטְתֵיהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Zeira took up the position of the father of Shmuel.
phrases.notes: His original view: permitted on the eighth day

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports how the two views of Step 15 were later held
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבוה דשמואל retracted to לוי's view. רבי זירא holds the original view of אבוה דשמואל.

steps.title: Proof from רבי זירא's ruling on a disqualified אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא ruled that an אתרוג that became פסול is forbidden to eat for all seven days. The phrase 'seven' implies that it is permitted on the eighth.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי זירא said: An אתרוג that became disqualified is forbidden to eat all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי זירא holds like אבוה דשמואל's original view by quoting his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא limits the restriction to 'all seven days.' He does not include the eighth day, so on the eighth the אתרוג is permitted, which matches אבוה דשמואל's original view. He even applies the restriction to an אתרוג that became פסול, because it was set aside for the whole festival.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on the eighth day: לוי (and later אבוה דשמואל) forbid the אתרוג even then. רבי זירא forbids it only through the seventh day, and he applies this even to a disqualified אתרוג.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Zeira said:
An etrog that became disqualified
is forbidden to eat all seven days.
phrases.notes: This implies that it is permitted on the eighth

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in Step 16 about רבי זירא's position
steps.raayaObject: That רבי זירא holds the original view of אבוה דשמואל (forbidden on the seventh day, permitted on the eighth)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא's ruling that a disqualified אתרוג is forbidden 'all seven days'

steps.title: Do not give the ארבעה מינים to a child on the first day
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rules that a person should not give his הושענא (his ארבעה מינים) to a child on the first day of יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: A person should not transfer ownership of his הושענא to a child on the first day of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a practical rule: on the first day of סוכות, do not hand your ארבעה מינים over to a child as a gift. The reason comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day of סוכות, the ארבעה מינים must belong to the person using them. Giving them to a child creates an ownership problem, and the גמרא is about to explain what that problem is.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the לולב bundle (the ארבעה מינים)
The first day of יום טוב

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
A person should not transfer ownership of the hoshana (lulav bundle)
phrases.notes: הושענא here means the ארבעה מינים, not the ערבה of הושענא רבה.

phrases.english: to a child on the first day of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: לָא לִיקְנֵי אִינִישׁ הוֹשַׁעְנָא לְיָנוֹקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After quoting רבי זירא's ruling about a פסול אתרוג, the גמרא brings another practical ruling of his.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not give one's ארבעה מינים to a child on the first day of יום טוב.

steps.title: Why not give it to a child?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי זירא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why giving the ארבעה מינים to a child is a problem. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance there seems to be no harm, since the adult can simply take the ארבעה מינים back. The question pushes us to find the hidden ownership issue.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logical basis for forbidding the gift to a child on the first day.

steps.title: A child can receive ownership but cannot give it back
steps.stepSummary: A child can acquire things but cannot legally transfer ownership. So the adult would end up using a לולב that is not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because a child can acquire, but he cannot transfer ownership. So it would turn out that the adult is fulfilling his obligation with a לולב that is not his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the problem. Once the child owns the ארבעה מינים, he cannot legally give them back, so the adult would be using a לולב that does not belong to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day, the תורה requires the לולב to be 'yours' (לכם). A child has the legal ability to receive a gift, but not to give one. So if the adult gives the ארבעה מינים away before using them himself, he can never get proper ownership back that day.

keyTerms.meaning: He cannot transfer ownership to others
A לולב that does not belong to him

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not giving the child a turn. The problem is transferring ownership to the child, because the child cannot transfer it back to the adult.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical source for the custom of an adult using the לולב first on the first day, and only afterward giving it to a child.

phrases.english: Because a child can acquire,
but he cannot transfer ownership.
And it turns out that he (the adult) fulfills his obligation
with a lulav that is not his.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּיָנוֹקָא מִקְנֵא קָנֵי, אַקְנוֹיֵי לָא מַקְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A child can acquire but cannot transfer ownership, so the adult would be left with a לולב that is not his on the first day.

steps.title: Do not promise a child something and fail to give it
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא teaches that one should not promise a child a gift and then not give it, because that teaches the child to lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said: A person should not say to a child 'I will give you something' and then not give it to him, because he will come to teach him lying, as it says: 'They have taught their tongues to speak lies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי זירא, also about children. Do not break promises to a child, because that trains him in dishonesty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching is placed here because it is connected to the previous one by author and topic: רבי זירא and children. It is not part of the אתרוג discussion. The פסוק from ירמיה shows that people can be 'taught' to lie by example.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught their tongues to speak lies (ירמיה ט:ד)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said:
A person should not say to a child
'I will give you something'
and then not give it to him,
because he comes to teach him lying,
as it is stated:
'They have taught their tongues to speak lies.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: לָא לֵימָא אִינִישׁ לְיָנוֹקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching of רבי זירא about children, attached because of the shared author and topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not promise a child something and then fail to give it, because that teaches the child to lie.

steps.title: רב and רב אסי on seven אתרוגים for seven days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links the dispute of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש to a parallel dispute: someone set aside seven אתרוגים, one for each day. רב says each one may be eaten right after its use. רב אסי says each may be eaten only the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is like the dispute of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, as it was stated: If someone set aside seven אתרוגים for the seven days, רב said: With each one he fulfills his obligation and eats it immediately. And רב אסי said: With each one he fulfills his obligation and eats it the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main topic: when may an אתרוג used for the מצוה be eaten? It brings a parallel dispute between רב and רב אסי, which matches the earlier dispute of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אתרוג is used for only one day. רב permits eating it as soon as its מצוה is done. רב אסי makes the person wait until the next day. This parallels the earlier dispute: ריש לקיש permitted the אתרוג even on the seventh day, while רבי יוחנן forbade it on the seventh day.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated (introduces an אמוראic dispute)

phrases.english: And this is like the dispute of Rabbi Yochanan
and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.
As it was stated:
If one designated seven etrogim for the seven days,
Rav said:
With each and every one he fulfills his obligation
and may eat it immediately,
And Rav Asi said:
With each and every one he fulfills his obligation
and may eat it the next day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side teachings about children, the גמרא returns to the question of when an אתרוג becomes permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: each אתרוג may be eaten right after its מצוה. רב אסי: only on the following day.

steps.title: What is the root of their dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רב and רב אסי disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the underlying reason behind the two opinions. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the אתרוג is set aside, which is called מוקצה. They differ only on how long that status lasts, and the גמרא wants to name the exact principle.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle behind the dispute in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The conceptual basis of the רב and רב אסי dispute.

steps.title: Set aside for the מצוה, or for the whole day
steps.stepSummary: רב holds the אתרוג was set aside only for its מצוה. רב אסי holds it was set aside for the entire day.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage (רב) holds: it was set aside for its מצוה. And the other Sage (רב אסי) holds: it was set aside for the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the root of the dispute: how long the אתרוג stays 'set aside.' Is it just until the מצוה is done, or until the day ends?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, once the מצוה is done, the reason for the set-aside status is over, so the אתרוג may be eaten right away. For רב אסי, the set-aside status covers the whole day, so even after the מצוה it stays forbidden until the next day.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: the אתרוג is set aside only for the מצוה, so it may be eaten right after. רב אסי: it is set aside for the whole day, so it may be eaten only tomorrow.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: it was set aside for its מצוה.
And the other Sage holds: it was set aside for the entire day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree on whether the אתרוג is set aside only for its מצוה or for the whole day.

steps.title: What do we do with two days of יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how communities outside ארץ ישראל, who keep two days of יום טוב, should treat the אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we, who have two days, how do we act?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question for חוץ לארץ, where every יום טוב is kept for two days because of doubt about the date. This sets up the answers of אביי and מרימר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside ארץ ישראל, the eighth day might really be the seventh day of סוכות, and the ninth day might really be the eighth. The question is how this doubt affects permission to eat the אתרוג.

keyTerms.meaning: Two days (of יום טוב in חוץ לארץ)

phrases.english: And we, who have two days,
how do we act?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנַן דְּאִית לַן תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי, הֵיכִי עָבְדִינַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the earlier rule (the אתרוג is forbidden on the seventh day and permitted on the eighth) to the two-day יום טוב of חוץ לארץ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the אתרוג is forbidden on the doubtful eighth day and the doubtful ninth day in חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: אביי: forbidden on the eighth, permitted on the ninth
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the eighth day, which might be the seventh, is forbidden. The ninth day, which might be the eighth, is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The eighth day, which is a doubtful seventh, is forbidden. The ninth day, which is a doubtful eighth, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that because of the doubt, the eighth day is treated like the seventh, so the אתרוג is still forbidden. On the ninth day it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the אתרוג is forbidden on the seventh day and permitted on the eighth. Since the eighth day in חוץ לארץ might be the seventh, אביי treats it strictly. The ninth day can be at most the eighth, so it is permitted.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The eighth, a doubtful seventh, is forbidden;
the ninth, a doubtful eighth, is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שְׁמִינִי סְפֵק שְׁבִיעִי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eighth day is forbidden because it might be the seventh. The ninth day is permitted.

steps.title: מרימר: permitted even on the eighth
steps.stepSummary: מרימר disagrees and permits the אתרוג even on the eighth day, even though it might be the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר said: Even the eighth day, which is a doubtful seventh, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר gives a different answer to the same question. He permits the אתרוג already on the eighth day in חוץ לארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרימר does not treat the doubt strictly. Since the eighth day is in any case שמיני עצרת, the אתרוג's set-aside status from סוכות does not carry over to it, even though (as step 32 notes) we still sit in the סוכה that day.
steps.whatToRemember: In חוץ לארץ, אביי forbids the אתרוג on the eighth day (a doubtful seventh) and permits it on the ninth. מרימר permits it even on the eighth.

phrases.english: Mareimar said:
Even the eighth, a doubtful seventh, is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרִימָר אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שְׁמִינִי סְפֵק שְׁבִיעִי מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's answer in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אתרוג is permitted even on the doubtful eighth day.

steps.title: What people actually did about the אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that in סורא people followed מרימר, while רב שישא בריה דרב אידי followed אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they acted like מרימר. רב שישא, the son of רב אידי, acted like אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how the argument between אביי and מרימר played out in real life. Different places and people followed different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In סורא they ate or used the אתרוג on the eighth day, following מרימר's lenient view. רב שישא was stricter and followed אביי, who forbids the אתרוג on the eighth day because it might really be the seventh. This shows the question was not settled yet, which sets up the final ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: סורא, a major Babylonian Torah center
רב שישא, son of רב אידי, an אמורא

phrases.english: In Sura they acted like Mareimar,
phrases.notes: They permitted the אתרוג on the eighth day.

phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi,
acted like Abaye.
phrases.notes: He treated the אתרוג as forbidden on the eighth day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports the practical behavior that followed the אביי and מרימר disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Practice was divided: סורא followed מרימר, and רב שישא followed אביי.

steps.title: The final ruling follows אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final decision: the הלכה follows אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In חוץ לארץ, the אתרוג stays forbidden on the eighth day, because that day might really be the seventh. It becomes permitted on the ninth day, which might be the eighth. מרימר's lenient practice is not the final הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, the אמורא whose view is accepted here

steps.whatToRemember: In חוץ לארץ, the אתרוג of the מצוה is forbidden on the eighth day and permitted on the ninth, like אביי.

phrases.english: And the halakha is like Abaye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the divided practice described in Step 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows אביי: the eighth day, which might be the seventh, is forbidden for the אתרוג.

steps.title: רב: the doubtful eighth day is seventh for the סוכה and eighth for the ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that in חוץ לארץ the eighth day counts as the seventh day for the סוכה and as the eighth day (שמיני עצרת) for the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said in the name of רב: the eighth day, which might be the seventh, counts as the seventh for the סוכה and as the eighth for the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new but related topic: how to treat the eighth day outside ארץ ישראל. רב gives a split answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because we are unsure whether this day is the seventh or the eighth, רב is strict both ways. We sit in the סוכה, in case it is still סוכות. But in our ברכות, such as קידוש, ברכת המזון, and תפילה, we mention שמיני עצרת, in case it is really the eighth day.

keyTerms.meaning: The eighth day, which might be the seventh
Regarding the מצוה of sitting in the סוכה
Regarding the ברכה, meaning mentioning שמיני עצרת in קידוש, תפילה, and ברכת המזון

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב is contradicting himself. He is not saying the day is both. Because of the doubt, he is simply being careful in both directions.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said
in the name of Rav:
The eighth day, which might be the seventh,
is the seventh with regard to the sukka
and the eighth with regard to the blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the אתרוג on the doubtful eighth day to the סוכה and ברכה on that same day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the doubtful eighth day: sit in the סוכה, as if it is the seventh, and mention שמיני עצרת in ברכות, as if it is the eighth.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the day is the eighth for both
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the doubtful eighth day counts as שמיני עצרת both for the סוכה and for the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: it is the eighth day for this and for that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב. He treats the day fully as the eighth day for both questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, this sounds like רבי יוחנן says we do not sit in the סוכה at all. That reading is exactly what the גמרא will correct in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
For this and for that, meaning both the סוכה and the ברכה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is the eighth for this and for that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רב's split ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubtful eighth day is treated as the eighth day both for the סוכה and for the ברכה.

steps.title: Everyone agrees we sit in the סוכה; setting up the real dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that everyone, even רבי יוחנן, agrees we sit in the סוכה on the eighth day. It then begins to say where they actually disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees that we sit in the סוכה. Where they disagree is...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן. It is setting up the next move, which will explain what they truly argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's words 'eighth for both' could make us think he says not to sit in the סוכה. The גמרא rules that out: sitting in the סוכה is agreed by all. So the dispute must be about something narrower, which the next passage will identify.

keyTerms.meaning: Sitting, here meaning sitting in the סוכה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's 'eighth for this and for that' does NOT mean we leave the סוכה. Everyone sits in it. The argument is about something else.

phrases.english: Regarding sitting, everyone agrees
that we sit in the sukka,
where they disagree is
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתַב כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּיָתְבִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the scope of the רב and רבי יוחנן dispute, ruling out a disagreement about sitting in the סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All agree that on the doubtful eighth day we sit in the סוכה; the dispute lies elsewhere.
